scope: Computer-use and GUI evaluations. Benchmark, offline-dataset, arena, and evaluation-suite artifacts are distinguished explicitly.

policies.comparison: Do not compare scores across different task versions, action spaces, observation modes, step budgets, scaffolds, attempt counts, or evaluators.
policies.launch: Earliest verified public artifact; precision is explicit.
policies.stars: GitHub stargazers_count for the declared official or shared host repository on the snapshot date; null is not zero.
policies.model_coverage: A family is listed only when a primary benchmark or model source reports an evaluated agent result. Harness support alone is not coverage.

evaluation_unit_definitions.static-grounding: One screenshot plus a target description; predict a point, box, element, or action.
evaluation_unit_definitions.offline-trajectory: Predict one or more actions from recorded GUI states without controlling a live environment.
evaluation_unit_definitions.interactive-episode: Act in a resettable live application until success, failure, or a step limit.
evaluation_unit_definitions.long-horizon-workflow: Produce and verify a multi-step or cross-application outcome, often with partial-progress checks.
evaluation_unit_definitions.arena-preference: Humans compare trajectories or outcomes; rankings are aggregated from pairwise preferences.
evaluation_unit_definitions.safety-adversarial: Measure unsafe action, policy violation, prompt-injection susceptibility, privacy leakage, or recovery.

benchmarks.output: Action prediction or trajectory with privacy-aware behavior.
benchmarks.metric: Privacy-risk and capability measures at action and trajectory levels.
benchmarks.environment: Cross-platform PC and Android trajectories.

benchmarks.name: CUAHarm
benchmarks.scale: 104 security-related tasks, including a 52-task harmful computer-use focus set
benchmarks.question: A potentially harmful computer-use request.
benchmarks.input: Desktop state and harmful or dual-use instruction.
benchmarks.output: Action trajectory, refusal, or safe response.
benchmarks.metric: Harmful completion, refusal, and utility/safety trade-off.
benchmarks.environment: Controlled desktop computer-use environment.

benchmarks.name: OSGuard
benchmarks.scale: Action-level safety items plus OSWorld-derived execution variants
benchmarks.question: Decide whether an action is allowed, unrelated, or unsafe, then execute tasks with explicit safety invariants.
benchmarks.input: Desktop observation, user goal, candidate/history actions, and hazard context.
benchmarks.output: Safety classification and/or safe computer-action trajectory.
benchmarks.metric: Action-level safety accuracy plus task utility and invariant violations.
benchmarks.environment: OSWorld-derived executable desktop tasks with injected hazards.

benchmarks.name: GUI-Robust
benchmarks.scale: Step-level and task-level GUI anomaly cases
benchmarks.question: Continue or recover when a realistic GUI anomaly disrupts the expected trajectory.
benchmarks.input: Perturbed GUI state, instruction, and action history.
benchmarks.output: Recovery action sequence.
benchmarks.metric: Action accuracy, coordinate accuracy, task success, and recovery diagnostics.
benchmarks.environment: Offline and executable GUI perturbation settings.

benchmarks.name: OS-Marathon
benchmarks.scale: 242 tasks across expense-reporting and transcript-recording domains; the project page also contains one inconsistent 252-task sentence
benchmarks.question: Process a scalable collection of receipts or transcript rows through a recurring professional sub-workflow.
benchmarks.input: Desktop files, office/browser applications, screenshots, and task instruction.
benchmarks.output: Repeated GUI actions and a fully populated persistent artifact/system state.
benchmarks.metric: Task completion across seven difficulty levels and seven executable environments.
benchmarks.environment: OSWorld-derived desktop plus fully functional task-specific applications.

benchmarks.name: MobileGym-Bench
benchmarks.scale: 416 parameterized templates: 256 test and 160 train, across 28 simulated apps
benchmarks.question: An everyday mobile task, including structured answer, navigation, payment, and high-risk variants.
benchmarks.input: Browser-hosted mobile UI, instruction, and action history.
benchmarks.output: Mobile-style GUI actions plus a typed AnswerSheet when required.
benchmarks.metric: Deterministic state-based Success Rate, Progress Rate, False Complete, and Unexpected Side Effects.
benchmarks.environment: Fully programmable browser-hosted mobile simulator; hundreds of parallel instances per server.
benchmarks.headline_result: 256-task test snapshot: Gemini 3.1 Pro 58.8% SR; Qwen3.6-Plus 45.7%; Qwen3-VL-4B 9.4% and 22.2% after GRPO.

benchmarks.name: AndroidDaily
benchmarks.scale: 350 tasks across 94 high-frequency closed-source Android applications
benchmarks.question: A realistic daily-use request in transportation, shopping, local services, entertainment, creation, social media, or utilities.
benchmarks.input: Live closed-source Android GUI, instruction, and visual trajectory.
benchmarks.output: Long-horizon mobile GUI trajectory and completed user-visible result.
benchmarks.metric: GRADE process-aware success using operational obligations, output quality, and negative constraints.
benchmarks.environment: Real-world closed-source Android applications without privileged internal state.
benchmarks.headline_result: GRADE reaches 87.37% human agreement; the strongest evaluated model reaches 62.0% success.

benchmarks.name: MementoGUI-Bench
benchmarks.scale: Long-horizon GUI trajectories curated for memory-control evaluation
benchmarks.question: Select, compress, retrieve, and use task-relevant multimodal history to choose the next GUI action.
benchmarks.input: Long screenshot/action history with text and ROI-level visual evidence.
benchmarks.output: Next action plus working/episodic memory decisions.
benchmarks.metric: MLLM-based semantic action matching, task progress, and memory consistency.
benchmarks.environment: Offline long-horizon GUI trajectories, evaluated alongside GUI Odyssey and MM-Mind2Web.

benchmarks.name: MobilePA-Bench
benchmarks.scale: 212 realistic mobile tools across 13 functional domains
benchmarks.question: A complex stateful mobile-planning request requiring tools, ordering, permissions, memory, skills, or sub-agent delegation.
benchmarks.input: Structured tool catalog, live application database feedback, user profile/memory, and task instruction.
benchmarks.output: Ordered tool calls, sub-agent delegations, skill invocations, and final verified state.
benchmarks.metric: Evidence-based state verification under strict tool-order, permission, and runtime-error conditions.
benchmarks.environment: Executable interactive function-calling sandbox with live application databases.

benchmarks.name: ScreenSuite
benchmarks.scale: Unified runners for ScreenSpot family, VisualWebBench, Mind2Web variants, AndroidControl, AndroidWorld, OSWorld, and others

benchmarks.output: Normalized grounding or agent action.
benchmarks.metric: Inherited component metric under a common model-evaluation harness.

benchmarks.question: Inherited from each component dataset.

benchmarks.metric: Component action/grounding metrics with common runners.
